workload.description: 24 multi-turn conversational requests, deterministic warm/cold mix: 8 resident (KVs on device), 8 host-memory, 8 SSD-cold; KV footprints ladder 16 MiB..2 GiB (3 cycles), interleaved arrival (tiers cycle SSD/resident/host). Sequential-server simulation: per-request service = tier load latency + prefill compute; TTFT = queue wait + load + prefill.

matched_baselines.description: FIFO arrival order (no residency awareness) vs residency order (tier separation resident->host->SSD, smallest-KV-first within tier) — identical workload, identical simulation, only the schedule differs.
matched_baselines.consistency_note: warm-tier p95 is identical across scenarios (8770.3 ms) as it must be: warm tiers never touch the SSD, so their schedule depends only on warm prefill compute. Cross-scenario invariance is a fixture-integrity check.
matched_baselines.claim: tier separation + size-ranked reordering cuts warm-tier p95 TTFT 1.73x (2 GB/s SSD) to 2.46x (500 MB/s SSD) and mean TTFT 1.14x-1.53x, with goodput unchanged by construction (identical total load bytes). The cold SSD tier absorbs the wait by design: its worst TTFT rises (11.9 s -> 15.2 s / 18.3 s -> 21.6 s) exactly because warm interactive users stop paying for cold loads.

metric_honesty.max_ttft_order_invariant: On a strictly sequential server the last scheduled request always waits for the whole makespan regardless of order. max/p99 TTFT are therefore order-invariant and are reported as such, not claimed as improvements. The order-sensitive metrics are mean TTFT and per-tier (especially warm-tier) worsts/p95.
metric_honesty.simulation: Per-tier load latencies are configured rates (host 20 GB/s; SSD 2 GB/s / 500 MB/s), not measured device I/O. Engine integration must replace them with measured Hanzo-hardware rates.

hypotheses.text: FIFO p95/mean TTFT under a mixed warm/cold queue is inflated by cold-load head-of-line blocking
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if load latencies were uniform across tiers, ordering could not matter and both schedules would coincide
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: FIFO warm-tier p95 pays 15.2 s (scenario 1) / 21.6 s (scenario 2) vs residency 8.8 s

hypotheses.text: tier separation + size rank reduces mean and warm-tier TTFT with unchanged total load bytes
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: fast-tier-first bias starving cold requests — measured: the cold tier's worst TTFT rises by design (11.9->15.2 s, 18.3->21.6 s); per-tier worsts are committed so the fairness cost is visible, not hidden
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: mean 1.14x-1.53x, warm-tier p95 1.73x-2.46x, goodput identical

hypotheses.text: the ordering itself costs orders of magnitude less than any real load latency
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: an accidental O(n^2) comparator would show µs+-scale per-request costs

out_of_scope: Bidaw mechanism 2 (response-predicted eviction): predicting user access patterns from LLM-generated responses needs response content and a storage trace a scheduling policy does not see
Bidaw mechanism 3 (selective storage-efficient history caching): footprint-vs-compute balancing across history tensors
real two-tier I/O: configured bandwidths, not measured device I/O — Hanzo-hardware rerun is the follow-up
GPU-side batching / continuous batching interplay (bounded sequential server only)
distributed/Enso gateway routing (Bounty #18) — covered by cloud PR #48 (Preble); this PR is the single-node half
